nodes.description: Subretinal AAV delivery of human CNGB3 under a cone-directed promoter. It rescued cone function in the canine and mouse models. In humans, the first-in-human AAV8-hCARp.hCNGB3 phase 1/2 trial (NCT03001310) was acceptably safe but showed no consistent efficacy change at 24 weeks, and intraocular inflammation was dose-limiting at the highest dose; an AAV CNGB3 vector from a second sponsor (AGTC-401, NCT02599922) has also been trialled. There is no approved gene therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Gene therapy rescues cone function in congenital achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Subretinal administration of rAAV5-hCNGB3 with a long version of the red cone opsin promoter in younger animals led to a stable therapeutic effect for at least 33 months.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term and age-dependent restoration of visual function in a mouse model of CNGB3-associated achromatopsia following gene therapy.
evidence.snippet: Therapy also resulted in long-term improvement of retinal function, with restoration of cone ERG amplitudes of up to 90% of wild-type and a significant improvement in visual acuity.

evidence.reference_title: First-in-Human Gene Therapy Trial of AAV8-hCARp.hCNGB3 in Adults and Children With CNGB3-associated Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: AAV8-hCARp.hCNGB3 for CNGB3-associated ACHM demonstrated an acceptable safety and tolerability profile.

evidence.reference_title: First-in-Human Gene Therapy Trial of AAV8-hCARp.hCNGB3 in Adults and Children With CNGB3-associated Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: There was no consistent pattern of change from baseline to week 24 for any efficacy assessment.

nodes.description: Total colour blindness in complete achromatopsia; patients cannot distinguish colours.

evidence.snippet: Achromatopsia is an autosomal recessive disorder featuring total colour blindness, photophobia, reduced visual acuity and nystagmus.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic basis of total colourblindness among the Pingelapese islanders.
evidence.snippet: Complete achromatopsia is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder characterized by photophobia, low visual acuity, nystagmus and a total inability to distinguish colours.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the CNGB3 gene encoding the beta-subunit of the cone photoreceptor cGMP-gated channel are responsible for achromatopsia (ACHM3) linked to chromosome 8q21.
evidence.snippet: Using RT-PCR and RACE, we identified and cloned the human cDNA homologue, designated CNGB3, which encodes an 809 amino acid polypeptide.

evidence.reference_title: CNGB3 mutation spectrum including copy number variations in 552 achromatopsia patients.
evidence.snippet: CNGB3 encoding the beta subunit of the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel in cone photoreceptors is the major achromatopsia gene.

nodes.description: Biallelic CNGB3 variants, most of them nonsense, frameshift, splice or copy-number changes that truncate or remove the protein, abolish the beta subunit of the cone cyclic nucleotide-gated channel. The recurrent c.1148delC frameshift accounts for most European mutant alleles, and Pingelapese achromatopsia is caused by a founder missense allele. This is the initiating, cone-autonomous lesion.

evidence.snippet: Two independent frameshift deletions establish that achromatopsia is the null phenotype of CNGB3.

evidence.reference_title: CNGB3 mutations account for 50% of all cases with autosomal recessive achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Thus, the majority of mutations in the CNGB3 gene result in significantly altered and/or truncated polypeptides.

nodes.description: Naturally occurring CNGB3 achromatopsia ("cone degeneration") in several breeds, with day-blindness and absent cone function in adults; the large animal model used for AAV gene-therapy development.

evidence.reference_title: Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Achromatopsia is characterized by reduced visual acuity, pendular nystagmus, increased sensitivity to light (photophobia), a small central scotoma, eccentric fixation, and reduced or complete loss of color discrimination.

nodes.description: Targeted Cngb3 knockout with early loss of cone ERG, reduced CNGA3, cone apoptosis and slow cone loss; rod function is preserved.
A later-onset progressive cone dystrophy, with deterioration of acuity, colour vision and photopic ERG from childhood or the second decade, is a recognised CNGB3 presentation.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive cone dystrophy associated with mutation in CNGB3.
evidence.snippet: Electrophysiological testing of these three subjects demonstrated clear evidence of progressive deterioration of cone responses over time; rod responses were normal.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive analysis of the achromatopsia genes CNGA3 and CNGB3 in progressive cone dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: In 3 arCD probands (3/60; 5%) we found 2 mutations in the CNGB3 gene.

nodes.description: The characteristic clinical outcome in complete achromatopsia: cone dysfunction present from early infancy with poor visual acuity, pendular nystagmus, photophobia and loss of colour discrimination in all axes, with preserved rod vision. Visual function is broadly stationary in most achromats even though cone structure is slowly lost.

evidence.reference_title: CNGB3 mutations account for 50% of all cases with autosomal recessive achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Achromatopsia is a congenital, autosomal recessively inherited disorder characterized by a lack of color discrimination, low visual acuity (<0.2), photophobia, and nystagmus.

evidence.reference_title: Long-term and age-dependent restoration of visual function in a mouse model of CNGB3-associated achromatopsia following gene therapy.
evidence.snippet: Although of early onset, its stationary character and the potential for rapid assessment of restoration of retinal function following therapy renders achromatopsia a very attractive candidate for gene therapy.

evidence.reference_title: REPEATABILITY AND LONGITUDINAL ASSESSMENT OF FOVEAL CONE STRUCTURE IN CNGB3-ASSOCIATED ACHROMATOPSIA.
evidence.snippet: Over the time scales investigated (6-26 months), achromatopsia seems to be a structurally stable condition, although longer-term follow-up is needed.

nodes.description: In CNG channel-deficient mouse cones, including Cngb3-deficient cones on a cone-dominant background, ER stress markers rise and cones die by an ER stress-associated apoptotic pathway. Work mainly in Cnga3-deficient mice implicates elevated cGMP/PKG signalling and up-regulation of the ER calcium channel RyR2 in driving this stress.

evidence.reference_title: Endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated cone photoreceptor degeneration in cyclic nucleotide-gated channel deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Along with these, up-regulation of the cysteine protease calpains and cleavage of caspase-12 and caspase-7 were found in the channel-deficient retinas, suggesting an endoplasmic reticulum stress-associated apoptosis.

evidence.reference_title: Potential contribution of ryanodine receptor 2 upregulation to cGMP/PKG signaling-induced cone degeneration in cyclic nucleotide-gated channel deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Findings from this work demonstrate the regulation of cGMP/PKG signaling on RyR2 in the retina and support the role of RyR2 upregulation in cGMP/PKG signaling-induced ER stress and photoreceptor degeneration.

nodes.description: Without a working cGMP-gated channel, the light-driven fall in cGMP has no conductance to close, so the cone cannot generate an electrical response to light. Cones remain present but silent; cone-driven (photopic and flicker) ERG responses are absent or nearly so, while rod-driven responses are normal or mildly reduced.

evidence.snippet: Combined with earlier findings, our results demonstrate that both alpha- and beta-subunits of the cGMP-gated channel are essential for phototransduction in all three classes of cones.

nodes.description: The native cone CNG channel is a heterotetramer of CNGA3 and CNGB3 subunits. Without CNGB3 the cone outer segment lacks a normally functioning cGMP-gated cation channel; in the Cngb3 knockout mouse CNGA3 protein and mRNA also fall, so the deficit extends to the ion-conducting subunit.

evidence.snippet: Thus this work provides the first biochemical evidence showing the inter-subunit interaction between CNGA3 and CNGB3 and the presence of heterotetrameric complexes of the native cone CNG channel in retina.

evidence.snippet: Notably, CNGA3 protein and mRNA levels were significantly decreased in CNGB3(-/-) mice; in contrast, mRNA levels of S-opsin, Gnat2 and Pde6c were unchanged, relative to WT mice.

evidence.reference_title: CNGB3 achromatopsia with progressive loss of residual cone function and impaired rod-mediated function.
evidence.snippet: The fundi of the affected subjects showed macular atrophy by middle age, while the carriers showed peripheral RPE granularity in childhood and macular atrophy in late middle age.

nodes.description: Nystagmus develops in early infancy in complete achromatopsia and is predominantly pendular in CNGB3 patients; it is typically absent in the later-onset progressive cone dystrophy subtype.

evidence.reference_title: Achromatopsia.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic basis of total colourblindness among the Pingelapese islanders.
evidence.snippet: Complete achromatopsia is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder characterized by photophobia, low visual acuity, nystagmus and a total inability to distinguish colours.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive cone dystrophy associated with mutation in CNGB3.
evidence.snippet: The clinical findings in one family member were consistent with a diagnosis of complete achromatopsia, with nystagmus, photophobia, and poor visual acuity from early infancy and complete color-blindness, normal fundi, and absent cone responses with normal rod responses on electroretinography (ERG).

evidence.reference_title: CNGB3 achromatopsia with progressive loss of residual cone function and impaired rod-mediated function.
evidence.snippet: All affected subjects had acuity ranging between 20/200 and 20/400, moderately constricted GVFs, normal DATs, reduced rod b-wave amplitudes, and extinguished photopic b-wave and flicker responses.

evidence.reference_title: Achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Best visual acuity varies with severity of the disease; it is 20/200 or less in complete achromatopsia and may be as high as 20/80 in incomplete achromatopsia.

nodes.description: Cones lacking a functional CNG channel are slowly lost. The Cngb3 knockout mouse shows early cone apoptosis and a cone density falling to about half of wild type by one year; patients show age-related progression from an intact to a disrupted and then absent foveal ellipsoid zone, with macular atrophy in adults. In the progressive cone dystrophy subtype, degeneration also produces progressive loss of cone function.

evidence.snippet: Multiple regression analysis showed a significant correlation of OCT stage with age (p < 0.001) and no correlation with gene (p > 0.05).

nodes.description: Missense alleles previously associated with macular degeneration. Both increased cGMP sensitivity when co-expressed with CNGA3 in Xenopus oocytes; the achromatopsia alleles P309L and G558C also showed enhanced channel activity there, so the oocyte phenotype does not separate the two clinical groups.

evidence.reference_title: Inherited macular degeneration-associated mutations in CNGB3 increase the ligand sensitivity and spontaneous open probability of cone cyclic nucleotide-gated channels.
evidence.snippet: With the exception of S156F, each of the mutant channels displayed electrophysiological properties reflecting enhanced channel activity at physiological concentrations of cGMP (i.e., a gain-of-function phenotype).

nodes.description: Recurrent frameshift allele, the most frequent CNGB3 variant in European achromats.

evidence.reference_title: CNGB3 mutations account for 50% of all cases with autosomal recessive achromatopsia.
evidence.snippet: Several mutations were found recurrently, in particular a 1 bp deletion, c.1148delC, which accounts for over 70% of all CNGB3 mutant alleles.

evidence.reference_title: Achromatopsia: the CNGB3 p.T383fsX mutation results from a founder effect and is responsible for the visual phenotype in the original report of uniparental disomy 14.
evidence.snippet: The most frequent mutation, p.T383fsX in CNGB3, accounted for 75% (18/24) of disease-associated alleles; intragenic SNPs in unrelated patients revealed transmission of a common haplotype consistent with a founder effect.

nodes.description: Deep-intronic variant that activates a pseudoexon; a recurrent second allele in single-variant patients.

evidence.reference_title: Deep-intronic variants in CNGB3 cause achromatopsia by pseudoexon activation.
evidence.snippet: Variant c.1663-1205G>A, found in 14 subjects, and variant c.1663-2137C>T, found in two subjects, were indeed shown to exert a splicing defect by causing pseudoexon insertion into the transcript.

nodes.description: Missense allele reported in progressive cone dystrophy in trans with c.1148delC, and homozygous in a cone-dystrophy proband who also carried two CNGA3 variants; a compound heterozygote with an 8-bp deletion had achromatopsia with extinguished cone ERGs.

evidence.reference_title: Progressive cone dystrophy associated with mutation in CNGB3.
evidence.snippet: All three individuals with this progressive phenotype were found to be compound heterozygotes for the 1148delC (Thr383fs) frameshift mutation and a novel Arg403Gln missense mutation in CNGB3.
